description:
## Mandatory context and boundaries
Read the parent epic first. Applicable owners: AGENTS.md; docs/agent-tools.md; docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md; docs/exec-plans/PLAN_STRATEGY.md; docs/action-reuse.md; docs/testing-approach.md; docs/services/channels.md (communication/Jido bridge and provider contracts); docs/services/engine.md (history, admission, finalization and delivery). Read docs/documentation.md before documentation/skill edits, docs/services/system-config.md before credential fixtures, and local module @moduledoc before extending a helper. Apply code-quality for code and skill-creator for the skill.
Only test/ additions or backward-compatible support changes, lib/mix/tasks/zaq.test.gen.channel.ex, and .agents/skills/add-channel-integration-tests/** are authorized. Do not edit application modules, dependency source/pins, config, migrations, mix.exs, CI, or unrelated skills. Existing-test expectation changes require the testing handbook's explicit approval; this epic authorizes additive coverage, not changing expectations.
Use real bridges, NodeRouter, Engine admission/history/persistence and configured Agent execution. Only provider/LLM boundaries are faked. A production defect is a reported blocker with a reproducer; do not patch production, silently omit a scenario, weaken an assertion, or close the issue as complete.
Validation timing, failure handling and final gates are owned by docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md. Record executed commands/results in this issue. No new browser E2E is needed: this work adds test/developer infrastructure without changing a deployed UI journey. No commit/push/merge authorization is implied.

Parent epic: zaq-o9d

## Functional specification and files
Own test/support/channels/integration/{case,fixtures,assertions}.ex, extend session.ex only for fields defined in the parent, and add harness-focused tests under test/zaq/channels/integration/.
IntegrationCase composes Zaq.DataCase with async: false. Session setup sequence:
1. Snapshot exact application-config values that the existing channel full-flow fixtures override, subscribe to relevant production completion events, and start the driver fake endpoint via start/1.
2. Start the existing local OpenAIStub server and deterministic response builder.
3. Create the connector using supplied connector_attrs; create linked active People through real fixture/context APIs; establish the named scenario's real permissions; create active/conversation_enabled configured agent and an IncomingMessageRouting rule.
4. Call driver.connect/2 with the saved connector and fixture context; complete readiness before returning Session.
5. On exit, stop this session's agent/runtime/listener and fake resources before sandbox owner shutdown; restore each env key including originally absent keys. Do not stop shared unrelated runtimes.
Use existing DataCase setup. Reuse AI credential fixtures and OpenAIStub/MultiAgentOpenAIStub; do not change IntegrationAgent.create!/4's conversation_enabled: false default. Build the channel-enabled fixture here.
Case/Assertions expose channel_session(provider, opts), emit_message(session, room, opts), await_exchange(session, emission, opts), read_transcript(session, person, transcript_id) with concise documentation. Driver callbacks receive the full session where required, keeping provider state opaque.
Completion must correlate exact connector/source/request/message ids. Capture native inbound processing completion and outbound Engine delivery-confirmation completion; final delivery attempts can be edits after status creation. Subscribe before triggering. No sleeps/polling or production test-only notifications. Existing PubSub/router events, synchronous ingress returns, bounded assert_receive and task/process completion are permitted. For async WhatsApp callbacks, a test-owned delegating observer may record real callback completion without replacing its implementation.
Support a scripted sequence of text LLM answers for follow-ups and a separate explicit tool-calling mode. Fail unexpected LLM routes/interactions with useful synthetic diagnostics.

## Tests to add before implementation
- Fixture agent is channel eligible; linked Person and connector-scoped rule resolve through real contexts.
- Setup success/failure cleanup, env present/absent restoration, resources stopped before Sandbox teardown.
- Two sessions use different endpoints/profiles/ids and correct sandbox ownership.
- await_exchange ignores unrelated connector events, separates typing/status/final response, and does not read confirmed history before completion.
- No-reply barrier can establish completed ingress before asserting no LLM/request/reply.
Use minimal fake external endpoints for harness tests; full provider round trips are added in later child issues.

## Branches/paths validated
Startup/readiness errors, LLM response/failure, created versus edited final answers, asynchronous completion, sandbox cleanup and concurrent-looking unrelated events in a sequential suite.

## Mocking plan
Only external provider and LLM endpoints. Real NodeRouter, Channels/Jido/Communication bridges, Engine, Agent and Repo. Do not create additional application seams or seed an answer/transcript that the test is supposed to produce.

## Documentation
Add lifecycle diagram and a complete minimal scenario example to test/support/channels/integration/README.md. Document async: false reasons and observations versus confirmed transcript state.

## Action reuse assessment
Reuse DataCase, credential/People/ChannelConfig/routing contexts, existing LLM mocks, real runtime startup and Conversations APIs. New orchestration helpers are local-only ExUnit code, not domain Actions. Inputs are synthetic fixtures and driver options; outputs are sessions/observed results; cleanup owns only its resources. No caller gains permissions from nil identity.

## Done when
Harness lifecycle tests pass and the public test helper API supports the parent contract without app/dependency changes. Existing helper defaults remain unchanged.

comments.text: Implemented Integration.Case, channel-enabled fixtures, canonical transcript assertions and an OTP public-call completion observer. Case uses existing LLM mocks, starts fake endpoints before connector creation, correlates completed Channels delivery to the persisted native input id, and restores exact application env state. Tests verify eligible agent/rule/Person setup, two isolated sessions, cleanup/env restoration, and completion filtering through real Channels.Api with no internal mocks. Validation: mix q (dev) passed; mix test test/zaq/channels/integration passed: 10 tests + 1 property, 0 failures. Native provider full-flow validation follows in .3-.5. All source edits remain under test/; existing assertions/default helper behavior remain intact.
